testable_competencies.interview_structure: Conduct a structured psychiatric history (identifying data, chief complaint, HPI, psychiatric functional inquiry including safety screening, past psychiatric/medical/substance/developmental history, collateral history) as the foundation for every psychiatric diagnostic objective in this chapter.

testable_competencies.mse_components: Perform and document a structured mental status examination (appearance/behaviour, attitude, speech, mood/affect, perception, thought process, thought content, insight, judgment, cognition), distinguishing key descriptive terms (e.g., circumstantial vs. tangential vs. flight of ideas; hallucination vs. illusion; delusion vs. overvalued idea).

entries.title: Approach to Psychiatric Assessment and Management Planning

testable_competencies.biopsychosocial_formulation: Apply a biopsychosocial framework (predisposing, precipitating, perpetuating, protective factors across biological/psychological/social domains) to formulate a psychiatric assessment and construct a management plan spanning biological, psychological, and social interventions.

entries.title: Suicide Risk Assessment and Management

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj59-1's key objective explicitly requires the candidate to 'pay particular attention to assessment of suicide risk and the potential need for urgent care' when assessing depressed mood; this unit is the chapter's dedicated, generalizable suicide-risk-assessment skillset (SAD PERSONS, ideation/plan/intent/means, hospitalization threshold) that operationalizes that requirement across all psychiatric presentations, not solely depressed mood.

testable_competencies.risk_screening: Screen every psychiatric patient for suicidal ideation using direct, non-judgmental questioning.
testable_competencies.risk_stratification: Stratify suicide risk using SAD PERSONS-type factors (demographics, psychiatric/substance comorbidity, past attempts, access to means, protective factors) and distinguish passive from active ideation with plan/intent.
testable_competencies.safety_disposition: Determine appropriate disposition (voluntary/involuntary hospitalization vs. outpatient safety planning) based on risk stratification and identify when urgent intervention is required.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps ELOM/legal content on involuntary admission (see SU-PS-49/51 Canadian Legal Issues) where hospitalization decisions intersect with Mental Health Act forms; this unit itself is the clinical risk-assessment skill, not the legal admission mechanism.

entries.title: Approach to and Differential Diagnosis of Psychosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj86's key objective directly requires diagnosing the cause of psychosis 'with particular attention to distinguishing primary psychotic disorders from other causes of psychosis, including delirium, psychotic disorder due to another medical condition, and substance/medication-induced psychotic disorder' -- this unit is exactly that differential-diagnosis framework.

testable_competencies.differential: Given a patient with psychosis, generate and prioritize a differential diagnosis distinguishing primary psychotic disorders from delirium, medical-condition-induced psychosis, and substance/medication-induced psychosis before attributing symptoms to a primary psychiatric disorder.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Schizophrenia is the prototypical primary psychotic disorder within the scope of obj86 ('Psychosis'); its enabling objectives (MSE with risk/capacity attention, investigations, voluntary/involuntary status determination, pharmacotherapy initiation, psychosocial planning) map directly onto schizophrenia-specific content.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize the diagnostic pattern of schizophrenia (positive/negative/cognitive symptom domains, duration criteria, functional decline) and differentiate from other psychotic disorders by duration and course.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate acute and maintenance management plan (antipsychotic pharmacotherapy, psychosocial supports, safety assessment).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj86's scope as a primary psychotic disorder distinguished from schizophrenia principally by duration (1-6 mo); the objective's general psychosis diagnostic framework applies, but obj86's illustrative causal-conditions list names schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder rather than schizophreniform disorder specifically, so evidence is MODERATE rather than STRONG.

testable_competencies.duration_differential: Distinguish schizophreniform disorder from schizophrenia and brief psychotic disorder principally by symptom duration (1-6 mo, vs. >6 mo for schizophrenia and <1 mo for brief psychotic disorder).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj86's differential for psychosis (duration <1 mo, often stressor-related, full return to baseline functioning); MODERATE because the objective does not name this specific subtype in its causal-conditions list.

testable_competencies.duration_differential: Recognize brief psychotic disorder as psychosis lasting <1 mo with eventual full return to premorbid functioning, often precipitated by a stressor, and differentiate from schizophreniform/schizophrenia by duration and prognosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj86's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'schizoaffective disorder' as an example psychotic disorder; the diagnostic and management framework of obj86 applies directly, requiring recognition that mood episodes and psychosis co-occur with psychosis persisting outside mood episodes.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia with mood symptoms and from mood disorder with psychotic features by the relative timing/persistence of psychotic vs. mood symptoms.
testable_competencies.prognosis_management: Recognize an intermediate prognosis between schizophrenia and mood disorder, and that management combines antipsychotics with mood stabilizers/antidepressants as indicated.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Delusional disorder is an explicit differential for psychosis within obj86's scope, distinguished from schizophrenia by preserved functioning outside the delusional theme and absence of prominent hallucinations/disorganization.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize delusional disorder (isolated, non-bizarre delusion(s) with otherwise largely preserved functioning) and distinguish it from schizophrenia by the absence of broader functional impairment and prominent hallucinations/disorganized thought.

entries.title: Mood Episodes (Major Depressive, Manic, Hypomanic, Mixed)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit is the foundational mood-episode taxonomy (episode types and their defining features) that underlies both obj59-1 (depressed mood) and bipolar-spectrum diagnosis; MODERATE because obj59-1 itself is scoped to depressed-mood presentations rather than the full episode taxonomy including mania/hypomania.

testable_competencies.episode_recognition: Distinguish major depressive, manic, hypomanic, and mixed mood episodes by their defining symptom/duration criteria, and recognize that a careful history (including ruling out substance/medical causes) is required before attributing an episode to a primary mood disorder.

entries.title: Depressive Disorders (Major Depressive Disorder, Persistent Depressive Disorder)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj59-1's key objective: 'Given a patient with depressed mood, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity and complications, and will initiate an appropriate management plan,' with explicit particular attention to suicide risk assessment (see SU-PS-04).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose major depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) using DSM-5-type symptom/duration criteria and grade severity.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate biopsychosocial management plan (pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, safety planning) and recognize indications for escalation of care.

entries.title: Postpartum Mood Disorders

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj80-2 covers postpartum care broadly (shared decision-making, integrating best evidence); this unit's specific focus -- differentiating baby blues from postpartum depression from postpartum psychosis and recognizing the latter as a psychiatric emergency -- is a real but narrower slice of the broader postpartum-care objective, so evidence is MODERATE.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Postpartum depression is a depressed-mood presentation within obj59-1's scope with a distinct postpartum-specific timing/risk context not explicit in the base objective's rationale.

testable_competencies.spectrum_differentiation: Differentiate baby blues (self-limited, <2 wk) from postpartum depression from postpartum psychosis by symptom severity, timing, and presence of psychotic features.
testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize postpartum psychosis as a psychiatric emergency requiring urgent assessment given risk to both mother and infant.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Obstetrics postpartum-care content and Pediatrics infant-safety considerations; this unit covers the maternal psychiatric diagnosis/risk-recognition angle.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Bipolar depressive episodes fall within the general depressed-mood diagnostic framework of obj59-1, but bipolar I/II/cyclothymia diagnosis itself (requiring recognition of manic/hypomanic episodes) is not the specific focus of obj59-1's rationale, which is written for unipolar depressed-mood presentations; no MCC candidate objective names bipolar disorder directly, so evidence is MODERATE via the shared mood-episode/depressed-mood framework.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose bipolar I disorder (>=1 manic episode), bipolar II disorder (hypomanic + major depressive episodes), and cyclothymia, distinguishing mania from hypomania by severity/duration/functional impairment.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize mood stabilizer pharmacotherapy as first-line and the risk of antidepressant-induced switch to mania if used without a mood stabilizer.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj69's key objective: 'Given a patient with anxiety, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications and will initiate an appropriate management plan'; panic disorder is a core anxiety-disorder presentation.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose panic disorder (recurrent unexpected panic attacks plus >=1 mo of persistent concern/worry about additional attacks or maladaptive behavioural change) and distinguish from a medical mimicker (e.g., cardiac, thyroid, pulmonary) causing panic-like symptoms.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate management (CBT with interoceptive exposure, SSRI/SNRI pharmacotherapy) and counsel that benzodiazepines are not first-line for chronic management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Agoraphobia is a distinct DSM-5 anxiety disorder (marked fear/anxiety about >=2 situations where escape may be difficult, e.g., public transport, open/enclosed spaces, crowds) within obj69's general anxiety diagnostic scope; MODERATE because it is not separately named in obj69's illustrative content and is frequently, but not always, comorbid with panic disorder.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize agoraphobia as an independent DSM-5 diagnosis (not merely a panic-disorder complication) and its characteristic situational avoidance pattern.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: GAD is the prototypical chronic-anxiety presentation within obj69's scope: excessive, difficult-to-control worry about multiple domains for >=6 mo with associated somatic symptoms.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose GAD (excessive worry >=6 mo, difficult to control, with associated symptoms such as restlessness, fatigue, concentration difficulty, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance) and grade severity/functional impact.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Social anxiety disorder (marked fear of social/performance situations involving possible scrutiny) is a DSM-5 anxiety disorder within obj69's general scope; MODERATE as it is not individually named in the objective's illustrative content.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize social anxiety disorder (persistent fear of social/performance situations due to fear of negative evaluation, causing avoidance or endurance with marked distress) and distinguish from normal shyness by severity/impairment/duration (>=6 mo).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Specific phobia falls within obj69's general anxiety-disorder diagnostic scope; MODERATE because the objective's illustrative content does not name specific phobia individually.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_management: Recognize specific phobia (marked, disproportionate, persistent fear of a specific object/situation, actively avoided or endured with intense anxiety, >=6 mo) and that exposure-based CBT -- not pharmacotherapy -- is first-line treatment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj123's key objective: 'Given a patient with obsessions and/or compulsive behaviour, the candidate will diagnose the condition, along with its severity and possible complications,' with attention to etiology and coexisting conditions.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose OCD using DSM-5-type criteria (obsessions and/or compulsions that are time-consuming or cause significant distress/impairment) and distinguish obsessions (ego-dystonic, unwanted) from delusions and from OCPD traits (ego-syntonic).
testable_competencies.management: Initiate first-line management (exposure and response prevention CBT and/or SSRI at OCD-specific higher dosing) and recognize refractory-disease escalation options exist without needing procedural detail.

entries.title: OCD-Related Disorders (Body Dysmorphic Disorder, Hoarding, Trichotillomania, Excoriation)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj123's title explicitly includes 'and related disorders'; MODERATE because the objective's key/enabling objectives are written around obsessions/compulsions specifically rather than the body-focused repetitive behaviours (hoarding, hair-pulling, skin-picking, dysmorphic preoccupation) that characterize this related-disorder group.

testable_competencies.pattern_recognition: Recognize the OCD-related disorder pattern (body dysmorphic disorder: preoccupation with perceived physical defect; hoarding disorder: persistent difficulty discarding possessions; trichotillomania: recurrent hair-pulling; excoriation disorder: recurrent skin-picking) and that each requires significant distress/impairment for diagnosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj128's key objective: 'Given a patient who has experienced psychological trauma, the candidate will diagnose the nature, severity, and complications... assess safety risks and the potential need for urgent care.' PTSD is the primary diagnostic endpoint of psychological trauma exposure.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose PTSD (exposure to trauma plus intrusion, avoidance, negative alterations in cognition/mood, and hyperarousal symptoms persisting >1 mo with functional impairment) and distinguish from acute stress disorder by duration.
testable_competencies.safety: Assess safety risk (including suicide risk, common in PTSD) and identify need for urgent care.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate management (trauma-focused psychotherapy first-line; SSRIs/SNRIs as pharmacologic option; prazosin can help trauma-related nightmares).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Adjustment disorder responds to an identifiable stressor (not necessarily meeting PTSD's trauma-exposure threshold) with emotional/behavioural symptoms out of proportion to the stressor; falls within the broader psychological-stress-response scope of obj128 but is a distinct, lower-severity diagnostic category, so evidence is MODERATE.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish adjustment disorder (emotional/behavioural symptoms within 3 mo of an identifiable stressor, resolving within 6 mo of stressor/consequences ending, not meeting criteria for another disorder) from PTSD, normal stress response, and major depressive disorder.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Complicated/prolonged grief with superimposed major depressive symptoms falls within obj59-1's depressed-mood diagnostic scope; MODERATE because normal bereavement itself is explicitly not a psychiatric disorder and the objective is not written specifically for grief.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Distinguish normal grief from complicated/prolonged grief or superimposed major depressive disorder, and recognize when grief therapy alone vs. added pharmacotherapy is indicated (comorbid MDD, past mood-disorder history, or severe symptoms).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj58-2's key objective: 'Given a patient with delirium, a candidate will recognize the syndrome, diagnose the cause(s), and will initiate an appropriate management plan,' with particular attention to the urgent nature of the condition.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize delirium (acute onset, fluctuating course, inattention, plus disorganized thinking or altered consciousness -- CAM criteria) and distinguish from dementia by acuity/fluctuation/attention.
testable_competencies.workup: Identify the underlying cause using a systematic approach (e.g., I WATCH DEATH categories) and initiate urgent management addressing the precipitant.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj58-3's key objective to identify potential causes/severity/complications of cognitive decline, look for reversible risk factors, and differentiate early Alzheimer disease from other causes.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish major from mild neurocognitive disorder by degree of functional independence, and delirium from dementia by acuity/course/attention.
testable_competencies.reversible_causes: Screen for and identify reversible/treatable causes of cognitive decline before attributing to a primary neurodegenerative process.

entries.title: Substance Use Disorders: General Approach and Diagnosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj103's key objective to identify substance use/addictive disorder, potential consequences, and need for immediate intervention/ongoing support.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Apply DSM-5 substance use disorder criteria (mild 2-3, moderate 4-5, severe >=6 of 11 criteria within 12 mo) uniformly across substances.
testable_competencies.history: Take a structured substance use history addressing use pattern, consequences, prior quit attempts, withdrawal, and functional impact.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This substance-specific unit instantiates obj103's general substance-use-disorder framework (SU-PS-27) for this particular substance class; MODERATE because obj103's own illustrative content does not name this substance specifically.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the characteristic intoxication/withdrawal presentation and health consequences of this substance.

entries.title: Alcohol Use Disorder, Intoxication, and Withdrawal

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Alcohol and opioid intoxication/withdrawal are the two substance classes in this chapter with well-defined, potentially life-threatening withdrawal syndromes (delirium tremens/seizures; opioid withdrawal), making them the highest-yield, most directly testable instances of obj103's 'need for immediate intervention' language.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj103-1's key objective to identify suspected substance withdrawal, potential consequences, and need for immediate/continuing support -- this substance has a clinically significant, potentially dangerous withdrawal syndrome.

testable_competencies.intoxication_withdrawal: Recognize the intoxication and withdrawal syndrome for this substance and initiate appropriate acute management (including withdrawal-severity-scale-guided treatment where applicable), given the risk of life-threatening complications.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Alcohol and opioid intoxication/withdrawal are the two substance classes in this chapter with well-defined, potentially life-threatening withdrawal syndromes (delirium tremens/seizures; opioid withdrawal), making them the highest-yield, most directly testable instances of obj103's 'need for immediate intervention' language.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj103-1's key objective to identify suspected substance withdrawal, potential consequences, and need for immediate/continuing support -- this substance has a clinically significant, potentially dangerous withdrawal syndrome.

testable_competencies.intoxication_withdrawal: Recognize the intoxication and withdrawal syndrome for this substance and initiate appropriate acute management (including withdrawal-severity-scale-guided treatment where applicable), given the risk of life-threatening complications.

entries.title: Cocaine Use Disorder and Stimulant Intoxication

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This substance-specific unit instantiates obj103's general substance-use-disorder framework (SU-PS-27) for this particular substance class; MODERATE because obj103's own illustrative content does not name this substance specifically.

entries.title: Amphetamine Use Disorder and Stimulant Intoxication

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This substance-specific unit instantiates obj103's general substance-use-disorder framework (SU-PS-27) for this particular substance class; MODERATE because obj103's own illustrative content does not name this substance specifically.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This substance-specific unit instantiates obj103's general substance-use-disorder framework (SU-PS-27) for this particular substance class; MODERATE because obj103's own illustrative content does not name this substance specifically.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This substance-specific unit instantiates obj103's general substance-use-disorder framework (SU-PS-27) for this particular substance class; MODERATE because obj103's own illustrative content does not name this substance specifically.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj124's key objective: 'Given a patient with prominent or vague somatic symptoms and significant distress causing disability, without consistent pathophysiologic findings, the candidate will consider a somatic symptom-type disorder.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose somatic symptom disorder (>=1 distressing somatic symptom plus excessive thoughts/feelings/behaviours related to the symptom, persisting >6 mo) as a diagnosis of inclusion (based on the disproportionate response) rather than pure exclusion of organic disease.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize that regular scheduled follow-up (not symptom-contingent visits) and avoiding unnecessary investigations are key management principles.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Illness anxiety disorder (preoccupation with having/acquiring a serious illness with minimal or absent somatic symptoms) is grouped with somatic symptom disorder in obj124's title scope; MODERATE because obj124's rationale is written around prominent somatic symptoms, which are minimal/absent by definition in illness anxiety disorder.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish illness anxiety disorder (preoccupation with having a serious illness, minimal/absent somatic symptoms, high health-related anxiety) from somatic symptom disorder (prominent somatic symptoms are the focus).

entries.title: Conversion Disorder (Functional Neurological Symptom Disorder)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Conversion disorder falls under the DSM-5 somatic symptom and related disorders chapter that obj124 covers by title; MODERATE because it is defined by neurological symptom incompatibility with recognized disease (a distinct mechanism from obj124's 'without consistent pathophysiologic findings' language for somatic symptom disorder) rather than by distress/disability from the symptom itself.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize conversion disorder (>=1 symptom of altered voluntary motor or sensory function that is clinically incompatible with recognized neurological/medical disease) and the importance of a genuine, careful neurological workup to rule out organic disease rather than a purely exclusionary diagnosis.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Neurology's approach to functional neurological symptoms; this unit covers the psychiatric diagnostic framework.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize dissociative identity disorder (disruption of identity with >=2 distinct personality states, recurrent gaps in recall) as a diagnosis strongly associated with severe early childhood trauma, without needing subspecialist-level diagnostic/treatment detail.

testable_competencies.differential: Recognize dissociative amnesia (inability to recall important autobiographical information, usually traumatic/stressful, inconsistent with ordinary forgetting) and the importance of excluding organic causes of amnesia (e.g., substance, head injury, neurocognitive disorder) first.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish depersonalization/derealization disorder (persistent or recurrent episodes with intact reality testing) from psychotic disorders (in which reality testing is impaired).

entries.title: Sleep-Wake Disorders (Overview, Sleep Hygiene, and DSM-5 Categories)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj98's key objective: 'Given a patient with a sleep disorder, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity and complications, and will initiate an appropriate plan for management.'

testable_competencies.differential: Given insomnia or excessive daytime sleepiness, generate a differential across the DSM-5 sleep-wake disorder categories (dyssomnias, breathing-related, parasomnias) and recognize characteristic distinguishing features (e.g., cataplexy for narcolepsy, snoring/witnessed apneas for OSA).
testable_competencies.management: Recognize sleep hygiene and CBT for insomnia (CBTi) as first-line for chronic insomnia, and that non-benzodiazepine agents are generally preferred over benzodiazepines when pharmacotherapy is used.

entries.title: Gender Dysphoria

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj94-1's key objective to provide respectful care and appropriate support/management for gender- and sexuality-related patient needs, in an unbiased, nonjudgmental way.

testable_competencies.recognition_counselling: Recognize gender dysphoria (marked incongruence between experienced/expressed gender and assigned gender, with clinically significant distress) and provide respectful, affirming initial counselling and referral, without needing gender-affirming procedural/hormonal protocol detail.

do_not_test: Specific gender-affirming hormone regimens or surgical technique (specialist/changing-guidance detail; see also PL chapter's Gender-Affirming Surgery unit).

testable_competencies.definitional_distinction: Recognize that a paraphilia becomes a paraphilic disorder only when it causes distress/impairment to the individual or entails harm/risk of harm to others, without needing forensic-psychiatry-level classification detail.

entries.title: Sexual Addiction / Compulsive Sexual Behaviour

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 94 explicitly lists sexual addiction under sexual disorders and requires an unbiased assessment with appropriate support and management.

testable_competencies.terminology: General awareness that compulsive sexual behaviour is a described but not formally DSM-5-recognized clinical pattern, distinct from paraphilic disorders.

entries.zero_question_reason: Retained as contextual terminology without independent question coverage; objective 94 supplies the MCC component anchor.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj94's key objective to address sexual dysfunction/disorder issues and offer appropriate support/management in an unbiased, nonjudgmental way.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize DSM-5 sexual dysfunction categories (desire, arousal, orgasmic, and pain disorders) and screen for contributing medical, psychiatric, and medication (e.g., SSRI) causes.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj118-2's key objective to diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of weight loss/eating disorder and initiate appropriate management, investigating for underlying medical conditions.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose anorexia nervosa (restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight or persistent behaviour interfering with weight gain, disturbance in self-perceived weight/shape) and grade severity.
testable_competencies.medical_instability: Recognize signs of medical instability (bradycardia, hypotension, electrolyte disturbance, arrhythmia risk) requiring urgent medical stabilization/hospitalization, and the risk of refeeding syndrome when nutritional rehabilitation begins.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj118-2's eating-disorders scope; MODERATE because bulimia nervosa is typically normal-weight/overweight (not the weight-loss presentation the objective's title foregrounds), though its diagnostic/management framework still applies.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose bulimia nervosa (recurrent binge eating with compensatory behaviours -- purging, laxative/diuretic misuse, fasting, excessive exercise -- at least weekly for 3 mo, in a patient often of normal or above-normal weight) and distinguish from anorexia nervosa binge-purge subtype by weight status.
testable_competencies.complications: Recognize medical complications of purging behaviour (electrolyte disturbance, esophageal/dental damage, arrhythmia risk).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls within obj118-2's eating-disorders scope; MODERATE because binge-eating disorder (recurrent binge eating without compensatory behaviour, often associated with weight gain) is not a weight-loss presentation, unlike the objective's title framing.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose binge-eating disorder (recurrent binge eating episodes with marked distress, at least weekly for 3 mo, without regular compensatory behaviour) and distinguish from bulimia nervosa by the absence of compensatory behaviour.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ARFID (food avoidance/restriction leading to nutritional deficiency, weight loss, or dependence on supplements, without body-image disturbance) falls within obj118-2's weight-loss/eating-disorder scope; MODERATE because ARFID's defining absence of body-image disturbance distinguishes it mechanistically from the anorexia-nervosa-centric objective framing.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish ARFID from anorexia nervosa by the absence of body-image disturbance/fear of weight gain, recognizing it can occur in children and adults for sensory, low-interest, or fear-of-consequence (e.g., choking) reasons.

entries.title: Personality Disorders (Clusters A, B, and C)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches obj75's key objective: 'Given a patient with a personality disorder, the candidate will differentiate between a personality disorder and other mental illness, recognizing the high prevalence of co-morbidities. The candidate will formulate an appropriate management plan.'

testable_competencies.cluster_recognition: Recognize the three personality-disorder clusters (A: odd/eccentric; B: dramatic/emotional/erratic; C: anxious/fearful) and their characteristic patterns, and differentiate personality disorder from an acute or comorbid Axis-I-type illness (e.g., Cluster A vs. schizophrenia by preserved thought organization and absence of sustained psychosis).
testable_competencies.borderline_pd_safety: Recognize borderline personality disorder's markedly elevated suicide risk and self-harm behaviour, and that dialectical behavioural therapy (DBT) is the principal evidence-based treatment.
testable_competencies.antisocial_pd: Recognize antisocial personality disorder requires a childhood-onset conduct disorder history and a minimum age of 18 for diagnosis.

entries.title: Child Development, Attachment, and the Child Psychiatric Interview

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj74-5 requires identifying normal developmental milestones/behaviours and addressing concerns; this unit's attachment-theory and interview-technique content is adjacent context for that broader well-child framework rather than the objective's own primary preventive-visit focus.

testable_competencies.attachment: Recognize the four attachment styles observed in the Strange Situation paradigm (secure, insecure-avoidant, insecure-ambivalent, disorganized) and their associated caregiver behaviour patterns.
testable_competencies.interview_technique: Adapt psychiatric interview technique to a child's developmental level (concrete, developmentally-appropriate language) and consider speaking with the child alone when appropriate.

entries.title: Mood Disorders in Children and Adolescents

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj59-1's diagnosis/management/suicide-risk framework applies to pediatric depressed mood; MODERATE because the objective's rationale does not address pediatric-specific presentation differences (irritable mood substituting for depressed mood) or pediatric SSRI black-box suicidality-monitoring requirements explicit in this unit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Complements obj74-5's developmental-surveillance framework when abnormal mood findings are identified and require investigation/referral.

testable_competencies.presentation_differences: Recognize that irritable mood may substitute for depressed mood in the pediatric MDD diagnostic criteria, and age-specific associated features (insomnia in children vs. hypersomnia in adolescents).
testable_competencies.safety_monitoring: Recognize the need for close follow-up when starting SSRIs in adolescents to monitor for increased suicidal ideation/behaviour.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Pediatrics' developmental/mental-health-screening content; this unit covers the psychiatric diagnostic/management specifics.

entries.title: Anxiety Disorders in Children and Adolescents

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj69's general anxiety-disorder diagnostic/management framework applies to pediatric anxiety presentations (including separation anxiety disorder, which is developmentally normal only in a bounded age range -- see SU-PS-52); MODERATE because obj69's rationale is not written with pediatric-specific presentation in mind.

testable_competencies.pediatric_presentation: Recognize pediatric anxiety disorder presentations (including separation anxiety disorder beyond the developmentally normal 10-18 mo window) and age-appropriate first-line management (CBT before pharmacotherapy in most cases).

entries.title: ADHD and Autism Spectrum Disorder (Cross-Reference to Pediatrics)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj5 covers attention/learning/school problems generally, encompassing ADHD; MODERATE because the TN Psychiatry chapter itself provides no ADHD-specific diagnostic/management content -- it is a pure cross-reference to Pediatrics P31, so this unit's own testable content is minimal.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC candidate objective specifically names autism spectrum disorder; obj21 (developmental delay) is the closest available registry match for a pervasive neurodevelopmental presentation, but ASD is not itself primarily a delay diagnosis, so this evidence link is weak and flagged for scope review.

testable_competencies.referral_awareness: Recognize that ADHD and ASD are neurodevelopmental disorders with their diagnostic/management detail owned by the Pediatrics chapter, and know the core recognition features sufficient to trigger appropriate referral.

entries.zero_question_reason: This chapter provides no independent ADHD/ASD content beyond an explicit in-text redirect to Pediatrics; testing this content belongs to the Pediatrics chapter's own study units to avoid duplicate coverage across chapters.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Primary content ownership sits with Pediatrics (ADHD: P31; ASD: P30); this unit exists only to account for the cross-reference bullets present in the Psychiatry chapter's Neurodevelopmental Disorders heading.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose ODD (pattern of angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behaviour, or vindictiveness for >=6 mo) and recognize disruptive mood dysregulation disorder supersedes ODD when both are met.

Diagnose conduct disorder (pattern violating others' rights/age-appropriate norms across aggression, property destruction, deceitfulness/theft, or rule violation) and recognize childhood-onset (before age 10) carries worse prognosis and higher risk of progression to antisocial personality disorder.

Recognize intermittent explosive disorder (recurrent impulsive-aggressive outbursts grossly out of proportion to precipitating stressors) and that it can be diagnosed alongside ADHD/CD/ODD/ASD when outbursts exceed what those diagnoses typically explain.

testable_competencies.modality_matching: Match common psychotherapy modalities (supportive therapy, IPT, CBT, DBT, motivational interviewing, group therapy, family therapy, mindfulness-based therapies, psychodynamic therapy) to their primary indications (e.g., DBT for borderline personality disorder and self-harm; motivational interviewing for substance use; CBT as first-line for most mood/anxiety/OCD presentations) at a recognition level, without needing technique-level protocol detail.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ECT is the fastest and most effective acute treatment for severe/treatment-resistant depression, a management option within obj59-1's 'initiate an appropriate management plan' scope; MODERATE because obj59-1's rationale does not name ECT specifically and ECT's indications extend beyond depression alone (catatonia, treatment-resistant schizophrenia/mania).

testable_competencies.indications: Recognize indications for ECT (treatment-resistant depression, depression with psychotic/catatonic features, situations where medications are unsafe or rapid response is needed -- e.g., high suicide risk, pregnancy, severe dehydration/cachexia -- refractory catatonia, treatment-resistant schizophrenia or mania).
testable_competencies.safety: Recognize ECT has no absolute contraindications and that its most clinically significant adverse effect is memory loss, which is usually transient.

testable_competencies.indications: Recognize rTMS as a noninvasive option with strong evidence for treatment-resistant depression, less effective than ECT for depression but with a more favourable adverse-effect profile (no anesthesia, no memory loss).

entries.title: Magnetic Seizure Therapy and Neurosurgical/Device-Based Treatments

testable_competencies.awareness: General awareness that magnetic seizure therapy, ablative neurosurgery, deep brain stimulation, and vagus nerve stimulation are experimental or last-resort options reserved for severe treatment-resistant depression/OCD unresponsive to standard treatment, without needing procedural or patient-selection detail.

entries.title: Other Somatic Therapy Modalities (Phototherapy, Aerobic Exercise)

testable_competencies.indications: Recognize phototherapy (bright light exposure) as first-line for seasonal affective disorder and adjunctive for non-seasonal depression, and aerobic exercise as an evidence-based monotherapy option for mild-moderate MDD and adjunct for moderate-severe MDD.

entries.title: Ontario Mental Health Act: Common Forms and Involuntary Psychiatric Assessment

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Involuntary psychiatric assessment/admission is the clinically operationalized exception to consent for a patient who lacks capacity and poses safety risk; falls within obj121-1's 'limitations, and exceptions to the requirement of consent' scope, but the objective is written generally and does not name Mental Health Act forms specifically, so evidence is MODERATE.

testable_competencies.threshold_recognition: Recognize the clinical threshold for initiating an involuntary psychiatric assessment (imminent danger to self/others, or incapacity for self-care due to apparent mental disorder), independent of the exact provincial form numbers/names, which are jurisdiction-specific and not to be hard-coded as generalizable fact.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantial overlap with ELOM's consent/capacity/involuntary-treatment content (see ELOM chapter); this unit provides the psychiatry-specific clinical trigger for invoking those legal mechanisms, not the general legal framework itself. Ownership (PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK/DISTINCT_CONTEXT) intentionally not finalized here per the chapter-scoping instructions, pending the global cross-chapter ownership audit.

entries.title: Consent in Psychiatric Practice (Cross-Reference to ELOM)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This heading is an explicit in-text redirect to the ELOM chapter's own consent content (ELOM12); obj121-1 is ELOM's own primary anchor for consent, already fully covered by the ELOM chapter's study units.

entries.zero_question_reason: Pure in-text cross-reference to the ELOM chapter with no independent content; consent is already scoped by the ELOM chapter's own study units, and testing it again here would duplicate coverage.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Primary content ownership sits with ELOM (ELOM12); this unit exists only to account for the cross-reference heading present in the Psychiatry chapter.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A CTO is fundamentally a consent-based (not involuntary-hospitalization-based) community treatment mechanism explicitly requiring consent of the patient or substitute decision-maker; falls within obj121-1's consent-exceptions/mechanisms scope, but the objective does not name CTOs specifically, so evidence is MODERATE.

testable_competencies.eligibility_purpose: Recognize the purpose of a CTO (structured community treatment plan for a patient with a pattern of relapse/readmission due to treatment non-adherence) and that it is consent-based with defined review rights, without needing exact provincial eligibility-criteria numbers as fixed fact.

entries.title: Duty to Inform/Warn (Cross-Reference to ELOM)
entries.zero_question_reason: Pure in-text cross-reference to the ELOM chapter (ELOM11) with no independent content; duty to warn/protect third parties (e.g., Tarasoff-type principles) is already scoped by the ELOM chapter's own study units.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Primary content ownership sits with ELOM (ELOM11), though duty-to-warn scenarios are especially likely to be vignette-tested in a psychiatric context (e.g., a patient disclosing intent to harm an identifiable third party); this unit exists only to account for the cross-reference heading present in the Psychiatry chapter.

entries.title: Landmark Psychiatry Clinical Trials (Reference Table)

testable_competencies.awareness: General awareness that landmark RCTs (e.g., CATIE, STAR*D) inform current psychopharmacology practice, without memorizing specific trial results/statistics.

entries.zero_question_reason: Per the chapter-scoping instruction not to hard-code specific trial results/treatment-sequencing detail at scope stage, and because difficulty should come from clinical reasoning rather than trial trivia; specific landmark-trial statistics are not generalist graduating-competency content.
